summary: Reproduced both MiMo streaming parser defects on the recorded base: normal text after a completed tool call remained in the detector buffer, and every split inside <tool_call> caused raw markup to be emitted as content. Updated the no-marker path to emit confirmed normal text while retaining only a suffix that can still become the opening marker. Added regression coverage for trailing and inter-call text plus all ten non-empty internal marker splits and partial-suffix buffering.

gpu_execution.evidence: The reported reproduction directly calls MiMoDetector and is deterministic CPU-only string parsing. No GPU execution was relevant or performed, and no model-serving inference is claimed.

remaining_limitations: No MiMo model weights or HTTP serving run was used; validation covers the actual detector implementation and neighboring parser tests, not model semantics or end-to-end generation.

The one-shot detect_and_parse implementation also omits normal text after a valid tool-call block on this base. That separate pre-existing behavior was observed in reports/j-a7df023cee8d/raw/reproduction-before.txt but was not expanded into this narrowly scoped streaming fix.
